rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Karmani contrasts hypocrites, whose inward states only God knows (with the Prophet informed by Him), with believers, whose outward obedience is seen by God, the Messenger, and fellow believers.
rows.anchor: جاء في (البرهان) للكرماني في هاتين الآيتين

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Karmani reads the hypocrites’ closing return to God as a threat, cut off from the preceding clause.
rows.anchor: جاء في (البرهان) للكرماني في هاتين الآيتين

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Karmani treats the believers’ return as a promise built on God’s seeing their deeds.
rows.anchor: جاء في (البرهان) للكرماني في هاتين الآيتين

rows.speaker: درة التنزيل
rows.claim: The cited reading says the Prophet was commanded to have believers perform visible duties; unlike concealed hypocrisy, these deeds can be seen by God, the Messenger, and believers, which explains naming the latter witnesses.
rows.anchor: وجاء في (درة التنزيل) أن الآية الثانية

words: إِلَّا كُتِبَ لَهُم بِهِۦ عَمَلٌ صَٰلِحٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 9:120 includes hardships such as thirst, exhaustion, and hunger that are not their actions, so it records a righteous deed for them; 9:121 lists their own spending and travel, needing no such phrase.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الآية الأولى فيها ما ليس عملاً لهم كالظمأ والنصب والمخمصة فهذه ليست من أعمالهم

words: إِلَّا كُتِبَ لَهُم بِهِۦ عَمَلٌ صَٰلِحٌ
لِيَجْزِيَهُمُ اللهُ أَحْسَنَ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Karmani says God counts unchosen hardships as the reward of a good deed, while actions in 9:121 are recorded as the deeds themselves; hence the first adds that phrase and closes with the reward of benefactors.
rows.anchor: جاء في (البرهان) للكرماني أن

words: إِنَّ اللهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
لِيَجْزِيَهُمُ اللهُ أَحْسَنَ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Karmani explains that 9:120 ends by affirming that reward is not lost because it includes hardships beyond their deeds, while 9:121 promises the best recompense for acts that were all theirs.
rows.anchor: جاء في (البرهان) للكرماني أن

words: إِلَّا كُتِبَ لَهُم بِهِۦ عَمَلٌ صَٰلِحٌ
إِنَّ اللهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
rows.speaker: درة التنزيل
rows.claim: Durrat al-tanzil says hardships are not the sufferers’ own acts, so God grants equivalent reward and does not waste the reward of those who obey and endure them; the added phrase is unnecessary for actual deeds in 9:121.
rows.anchor: وجاء في (درة التنزيل)

words: إِنَّ اللهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
لِيَجْزِيَهُمُ اللهُ أَحْسَنَ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
rows.speaker: درة التنزيل
rows.claim: Durrat al-tanzil distinguishes the endings: the first compensates those who encounter imposed hardship while obeying God, whereas the second promises good recompense for deeds they performed.
rows.anchor: وجاء في (درة التنزيل)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse assigns sin to the heart because testimony is held there and concealing it means keeping it within the heart; this makes the wording especially apt.
rows.anchor: ولم كتف بقوله: (إنه آثم) بل إسند الإثم إلى القلب وذلك لأنَّ الشهادة محلها القلب وكتمانها هو أن يبقيها في قلبه

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf asks why the verse names the heart when the whole person is sinful, then explains that concealment resides there, attaching sin to its organ is emphatic, the heart leads the body, and the wording prevents limiting concealment to the tongue.
rows.anchor: جاء في (الكشاف) في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqara and al-A‘raf add kānū because they describe Israelites of the past; Āl ʿImrān omits it because its example is a parable, not a report about an extinct people.
rows.anchor: فناسب ذكر (كان) في آيتي البقرة والأعراف دون آية آل عمران

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Karmani confirms that the Baqara and al-A‘raf verses report about a people who died and disappeared, whereas the Āl ʿImrān passage is a parable.
rows.anchor: جاء في (البرهان) للكرماني أن ما في السورتين يعني البقرة والأعراف "إخبارٌ عن قوم ماتوا وانقرضوا وما في آل عمران مَثَل"

words: وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّن شَيْءٍ فَمَتَاعُ الْحَيَوٰةِ الدُّنْيَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qasas mentions adornment because Qarun later appears before his people in it; al-Shura has no comparable worldly scene, so the addition suits the former context.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد ذكر الزينة في القصص لورودها فيما بعد

words: وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّن شَيْءٍ فَمَتَاعُ الْحَيَوٰةِ الدُّنْيَا
rows.speaker: معترك الأقران
rows.claim: Ma‘tarak al-aqran likewise connects the added adornment to Qarun’s story, where it makes the verse fit the narrative; al-Shura contains no such worldly episode.
rows.anchor: جاء في (معترك الأقران)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that Āl ʿImrān adds “nor will He look at them,” absent from Baqara, and begins to signal two reasons; the excerpt ends before giving them.
rows.anchor: فقد زاد في آل عمران: (ولا ينظر إليهم) بخلاف البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Qur’anic story has several lessons and evidentiary uses; it is not literally repeated, since each occurrence brings forward the aspect suited to its context and purpose.
rows.anchor: وهذا شأن القصص القرآني، فأنت ترى أن القصة في القرآن كأنها تتكرر في أكثر من موطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of Moses shows that God’s decree cannot be altered: Pharaoh killed Israelite boys to prevent his downfall, yet raised in his own house the person destined to end his rule.
rows.anchor: بيان أن قدر الله ماضٍ لا محالة وأنه لا يستطيع أحد أن يغيره أو يرجئه مهما حاول واتخذ من أسباب ووسائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ story also displays the terrible end of Pharaoh as the consequence of injustice and unjust rulers.
rows.anchor: ومنها: بيان عاقبة الظُلم والظالمين، ويتجلى ذلك في نهاية فرعون النهاية الوبيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites’ formation in humiliation, cowardice, and worldliness explains their resistance to Moses’ reform; after forty years in the wilderness that generation died and a differently formed generation emerged.
rows.anchor: ذكر نفسية وتكوين بني إسرائيل الذين تربوا على الذلة والجبن والخنوع وذكر عنادهم وصَلَفِهم وجُبنهم وحبهم للدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once known and believed, truth has irresistible power against enticement and threat, shown by the sorcerers’ belief in Moses and the faith of Pharaoh’s wife.
rows.anchor: بيان أن الحق له السطان الأعظم على النفوس إذا ما عرفته وآمنت به، وأنه ليس بوسع أيّ أحد أن يحول بينها وبينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an adapts each story to its context by omitting some details, expanding or summarizing others, changing sequence, and varying expression without changing the meaning.
rows.anchor: بل تراه أحياناً يغير في التعبيرات ونظم الكلام تغييراً لا يخل بالمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salvation in the afterlife has degrees; guarding against misguidance is a demanding, high rank, so each action and chosen word is placed where it fits.
rows.anchor: فمجاهدة الضلال والتحري لعدم الوقوع فيه مرتبة عالية تتطلب جهداً كبيراً ومشقة في العمل

words: فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ لَمْ يَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ
لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِۦ وَيُسَبِّحُونَهُۥ وَلَهُۥ يَسْجُدُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-A‘raf links the Adam story to its ending: the angels do not act arrogantly and do prostrate, unlike Iblis, whom the story portrays as arrogant and not among the prostrators.
rows.anchor: وقال في خاتمة السورة: {إِنَّ الذين عِندَ رَبِّكَ لاَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَيُسَبِّحُونَهُ وَلَهُ يَسْجُدُونَ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqara similarly links Iblis being among the disbelievers with the sūra’s closing prayer for victory over the disbelieving people.
rows.anchor: وقال في البقرة في إبليس: {وَكَانَ مِنَ الكافرين} وقال في خاتمة السورة: {فانصرنا عَلَى القوم الكافرين}

words: وَعَن شَمَآئِلِهِمْ وَلاَ تَجِدُ أَكْثَرَهُمْ شَاكِرِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis vows to obstruct human gratitude, matching al-A‘raf’s opening that people give little thanks; their following him, apart from believers, fulfills his aim, though their father Adam had also yielded to temptation.
rows.anchor: فقد قطع إبليس عهداً على نفسه بأنه سيحول بين بني آدم والشكر

words: لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s aim in whispering was to expose Adam and his wife; after they ate, their nakedness appeared and they covered it with leaves, making the following verse about clothing apt.
rows.anchor: فذكر أن الغرض من الوسوسة هو أن يبدي لهما السوءات المخيفة. وقد وقع ذلك فعلاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads clothing of piety as covering inward nakedness, while clothing and adornment cover outward nakedness, matching the preceding story.
rows.anchor: فالتقوى لبس يواري السوءات الباطنة، واللباس والرياش يواري السوءات الظاهرة

rows.speaker: التفسير الكبير
rows.claim: The cited commentary says God followed Adam’s exposure and leaf covering with the account of clothing, showing the great favor of enabling people to cover their nakedness.
rows.anchor: جاء في (التفسير الكبير) : "إنه تعالى لما ذكر واقعة آدم في انكشاف العورة أنه كان يخصف الورق عليها

words: لَا يَفْتِنَنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَٰنُ كَمَآ أَخْرَجَ أَبَوَيْكُم مِّنَ الْجَنَّةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning to Adam’s descendants recalls Satan’s expulsion of their parents by removing their clothing to reveal their nakedness.
rows.anchor: ثم انظر إلى تحذير الله لذرية آدم وكيف يتناسب وما مر فقال: {يابنيءَادَمَ لاَ يَفْتِنَنَّكُمُ الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to wear adornment at every mosque follows naturally because adornment means clothing and raiment; the next verse asks who forbade God’s adornment and wholesome provisions.
rows.anchor: وانظر بعد ذلك كيف أمر بأخذ الزينة عند كل مسجد فقال: {يابنيءَادَمَ خُذُواْ زِينَتَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ}

words: لَهُم مِّن جَهَنَّمَ مِهَادٌ وَمِن فَوْقِهِمْ غَوَاشٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence ends with Hell’s bedding and coverings: Satan stripped the parents in the Garden and seeks to strip their descendants outwardly and inwardly in this life, while the afterlife clothes them in Hell’s garments and coverings.
rows.anchor: إلا بأن نتسربل من سراسبيل جهنم أعاذنا الله منها وأن يكون لنا منها مهاد وغواشٍ
